html:
The Chapultepec Peace Accords were signed in Mexico City on 16 January 1992 by the government of El Salvador and the guerrillas of the FMLN, ending the Salvadoran Civil War.

Talks led by the United Nations had begun after the guerrilla offensive of 1989 and the end of the Cold War. The accords cut the army by half, abolished the security police that had run death squads, set up a new civilian police, and created a truth commission. The guerrillas laid down their arms and became a party named after Farabundo Martí.

The UN mission in El Salvador was one of the first large peace operations of its kind. The accords held, and elections followed, but land and poverty were left largely untouched, and gang violence later took the place of political war.
sum: The Chapultepec Peace Accords were signed in Mexico City on 16 January 1992 by the government of El Salvador and the guerrillas of the FMLN, ending the Salvadoran Civil War.
